nearbyCountiesFullText.description:
* WHAT...Locally slippery travel due to lake effect snow expected.
Localized snow totals in excess of 3 inches expected.

* WHERE...In Illinois, Eastern Will and Southern Cook Counties. In
Indiana, Lake IN County.

* WHEN...Until noon CST today.

* IMPACTS...Plan on locally slippery road conditions including during
this morning's commute.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Impacts from snow during lake effect snow are
often highly variable across short distances. Conditions may vary
from wet roads to snow-covered roads across just a mile. In
addition, snow will struggle to stick within a few miles of the
Lake Michigan shoreline.
nearbyCountiesFullText.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
for Illinois can be obtained at www.gettingaroundillinois.com. The
latest road conditions for Indiana can be obtained at
https://511in.org.

Be prepared for slippery roads. Slow down and use caution while
driving. If you are going outside, watch your first few steps taken
on stairs, sidewalks, and driveways. These surfaces could be icy and
slippery, increasing your risk of a fall and injury.

During lake effect snow, the weather can vary from bands of locally
heavy snow to dry weather just a few miles away. Visibilities can
also vary greatly. Be prepared for rapid changes in weather,
visibility, and road conditions.

FXUS63 KIWX 130819
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
319 AM EST Fri Nov 13 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Light lake effect/enhanced rain showers, possibly mixed with
  some snow, will continue early this morning across southwest 
  Lower Michigan and northwest Indiana. No snow accumulation is 
  expected as most of the lake effect precipitation will remain 
  anchored across extreme northwest Indiana/far northeast 
  Illinois.

- A more dominant band of lake effect rain and snow showers is expected
  to shift east into northwest Indiana and southwest Lower 
  Michigan late tonight into Saturday morning. Some localized 
  light snow accumulations of less than an inch are possible 
  inland and mainly across grassy areas. 

- Below normal temperatures continue today through the weekend
  followed by slowly moderating temperatures into the mid and
  upper 50s by the middle of next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 318 AM EST Fri Nov 13 2026

Dominant single lake effect band continues to affect extreme NW 
Indiana early this morning in the Gary vicinity. Some synoptic 
enhanced light precipitation extends east across the local area from 
South bend vicinity into southern Lower Michigan. This area of light 
precip appears tied to a lagging secondary low level baroclinic zone 
and weak accompanying low level frontogenesis forcing. Through the 
morning, this band of precip should tend to diminish with near term 
low level fgen progs depicting some weakening of this synoptic 
forcing. 

The dominant band across far NW Indiana may try to exhibit some 
slight eastward adjustment after daybreak as a broader synoptic 
scale upper level short wave drops south across the Mid MS Valley. 
Some subtle uptick in low level fgen forcing could aid in some 
eastward development this morning as 950-900 mb speed convergence 
associated with better northerly flow working south across western 
Great Lakes interacts with thermally modified mass fields over 
far southern Lake Michigan. The more pronounced low level cold 
advection this morning working across the western shore of Lake 
Michigan will continue to allow for development of a weak 
northerly low level jet across western Lake Michigan and a 
pronounced horizontal shearing zone across the western third of 
the lake. This should keep the higher precip rates and dominant 
single band anchored along this horizontal shearing instability 
axis through the morning hours to the west of the local area. 
With some uncertainty in other synoptic factors coming into play
discussed above, did maintain some low to mid range chance PoPs
extreme west, but not expecting any snow accumulation locally 
at this time.

By this afternoon southward passage of another upper level trough 
across the western Great Lakes will likely allow for better lake 
effect precip to shift back to the Chicago metro area into portions 
of far NW Indiana. Did maintain high chance/low likely rain PoPs 
across far western portions of the forecast area this afternoon, but 
it is possible this can be adjusted downward depending on trends. 
Otherwise for today, little temperature recovery is expected given 
weak ongoing cold advection and cloud cover. Between clouds across 
the west and a possible maintenance of higher cloud cover in east 
with Lake Huron connection, a zone from southwest Lower Michigan 
into the US-15 corridor could experience some sun today. Highs will 
likely be limited to the low-mid 40s.

For tonight, there should be a lull in the parade of stronger short 
waves rotating through the broad negative upper height anomaly which 
should allow for some backing of the flow to eventually take better 
lake effect precip chances into NW Indiana/SW Lower MI later tonight 
into Saturday AM. Thermal profiles and sfc/near sfc wet bulbs do 
appear on the marginal side of rain vs snow in modified airmass 
downwind of warmer Lake Michigan waters. It also appears by late 
tonight, some drying of the DGZ should take place which will make 
snowfall production less efficient and possibly promote more of a 
cellular character. Did maintain some light accums across La Porte 
of less than a half inch across mainly grassy areas farther inland, 
but currently not expecting any significant travel impacts. Lake 
effect rain showers in scattered fashion may continue into midday 
Saturday but should become less organized and cellular through time.

A weak short wave spilling down the central CONUS/south central 
Canadian ridge may cause some isolated-scattered light lake effect 
rain again by Saturday evening, but otherwise dry conditions are 
expected through the remainder of the weekend as a stable longwave 
pattern featuring central CONUS ridging remains established. This 
pattern will be characterized by weak baroclinicity and little day 
to day thermal advection. This will promote continued below normal 
temperatures through the weekend. Looking ahead to next week, the 
broad eastern CONUS negative upper height anomaly should finally 
begin to break down allowing for eastward progression of the 
longwave ridge as stronger Pacific systems moves inland. 
Temperatures should moderate back to above normal in this pattern 
for middle and latter portions of next work week. While thee are 
some indications a stronger eastern Pacific wave will dampen the 
longwave ridge, better quality low level moisture should remain 
confined to the southern/central Plains so a dry forecast has been 
maintained through this forecast valid period.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z SATURDAY/...
Issued at 1244 AM EST Fri Nov 13 2026

Predominantly MVFR conditions at the terminals, with potential
for IFR briefly at KSBN with rain showers over the next couple 
hours. Otherwise, continued northerly flow with gradual
improvement to more persistent VFR conditions.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 7 AM EST Saturday for LMZ043-046.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Marsili
AVIATION...MCD

spc.text:
SPC AC 130510

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1110 PM CST Thu Nov 12 2026

   Valid 131200Z - 141200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not forecast across the U.S. today and
   tonight.

   ...Synopsis...

   An upper shortwave trough near the California coast this morning
   will shift east toward the southern Rockies by Saturday morning.
   Cooling aloft will support weak instability across portions of
   southern AZ/NM to Far West TX. Boundary layer moisture is expected
   to remain modest, with the dewpoints generally in the 40s and 50s F.
   This will support scattered thunderstorms during the afternoon
   across southern AZ/NM, spreading eastward toward southwest TX by
   late afternoon/early evening. Southerly deep-layer flow is forecast,
   with effective shear magnitudes generally around 20-25 kt. Modest
   shear and instability will likely limit severe potential, though
   gusty winds and small hail could occur with the strongest storms. 

   Additional thunderstorms are possible across portions of coastal OR
   into northern/central CA as a second upper shortwave trough moves
   inland across the Pacific Northwest and Great Basin. A lightning
   flash or two is possible during the nighttime hours from central CA
   into the Great Basin, but overall coverage is expected to remain
   less than 10 percent.

   ..Leitman/Chalmers.. 11/13/2026

spc.text:
SPC AC 130657

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1257 AM CST Fri Nov 13 2026

   Valid 141200Z - 151200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are unlikely across the U.S. Saturday and
   Saturday night.

   ...Southern Plains...
   A mid-level trough over the western US is forecast to deamplify, as
   the primary shortwave continues southeastward across the southern
   Rockies/Plains. To the west, another trough will deepen across the
   Pacific coast while surface high pressure with cool and relatively
   dry conditions dominates the East. As the upper trough migrates
   across the Rockies and into the Plains Saturday/Saturday night,
   strong mid-level ascent will deepen a lee cyclone from southeastern
   CO into NM and West TX. Southerly flow will increase and modest
   surface moisture return (40s to near 50 F dewpoints) will occur
   beneath cooling mid-level temperatures over the southern High
   Plains. Weak destabilization is expected with model profiles showing
   perhaps up to 500 J/kg of elevated MUCAPE available.

   Ascent from the upper trough and increasing low-level warm air
   advection will likely support scattered thunderstorms from the Four
   Corners to OK/TX from Saturday afternoon/evening. A 30-40 kt
   southerly low-level jet over parts of western OK/TX may also aide in
   additional convection overnight. Some potential for a few stronger
   storms may exist if sufficient buoyancy and around 30-40 kts of
   effective shear develop. Likely elevated, marginally severe hail
   would be the primary hazard with any stronger storms able to
   persist. However the scant destabilization casts significant
   uncertainty on severe potential, as such, probabilities will be
   withheld for now. 

   Elsewhere, occasional lightning flashes will be possible along the
   Pacific Northwest coast ahead of the aforementioned upper trough.
   Additional storms are also possible along the lower TX Gulf coast
   within the southerly return flow and warm advection regime. Very
   weak buoyancy is expected and coverage, as well as any severe
   potential will remain low in both locales.

   ..Lyons.. 11/13/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 130828

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0228 AM CST Fri Nov 13 2026

   Valid 151200Z - 161200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS SOUTHERN
   AND CENTRAL TEXAS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms are possible across central
   and the south Texas to the Gulf Coast.

   ...Synopsis...
   A shortwave trough and mid-level jet will move from the southern
   High Plains into central TX beneath a building ridge over the
   Midwest Sunday. An associated surface low will aid southerly flow
   drawing a modified Gulf air mass northward across south-central TX.
   However, the expansive surface high to the northeast will likely
   stall the northward advance of the more robust surface moisture
   farther south. Elevated buoyancy and thunderstorms are likely across
   the Red River Vicinity with additional thunderstorm development
   possible farther south through Sunday and into early Monday.

   ...South-central TX to the Gulf Coast...
   Showers and thunderstorms are likely to be ongoing at the start of
   the period near the center of the upper trough and surface low
   associated with low-level warm air advection. Multiple rounds of
   showers and storms, in combination with the increasingly strong
   northerly surface gradient, should gradually focus the effective
   warm sector farther south into TX. Elevated buoyancy of a few
   hundred J/kg may persist across the Red River vicinity through
   Sunday afternoon, with low-end potential for sporadic hail with any
   stronger elevated storms.

   Farther south, more robust inland moisture return is expected with
   mid to upper 60s F surface dewpoints. As the upper trough
   approaches, low-level warm air advection and diurnal destabilization
   should support an increase in thunderstorm activity across parts of
   south and central Texas eastward to the lower to middle Texas Coast.
   Gradually strengthening veering wind profiles (EBWD 30-40 kt) may
   favor storm organization into clusters or transient supercells.
   Damaging gusts, some hail and perhaps a brief tornado are possible
   into early Monday.

   ..Lyons.. 11/13/2026
